engagement.short: Rat lung oedema and thymus readouts

engagement.model: Rat allergic airway inflammation (lung oedema; thymic involution as systemic index)
engagement.note: AZD5423 cut allergen-induced sputum eosinophils 61-63% at 7 h in 20 mild asthmatics; the rat lung-inflammation readout moved in dosed humans.
engagement.quote: AZD5423 300 and 75 μg significantly attenuated allergen-induced sputum eosinophilia by 63 and 61% at 7 hours, respectively, and by 46 and 34% at 24 hours after allergen challenge, respectively, versus placebo (all P < 0.05).

engagement.judgement: The rat model's readout is airway inflammation (plasma exudation/oedema); the human readout is sputum eosinophilia after allergen, a different quantity on the same axis, so magnitude is direction_only. Comparison paired by the drafter (Gauvreau cites the sponsor's preclinical work but does not set the rat data beside the patient data). Downstream tier: eosinophils and FeNO sit well below GR occupancy. Systemic-GR engagement also showed in humans as dose-related 24-h cortisol suppression in healthy volunteers (Werkström 2016, https://doi.org/10.1111/bcpt.12621; Prothon 2022, https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S334960), the human counterpart of the rat thymus index.
engagement.magnitude_basis: airway inflammation: rat lung oedema vs human sputum eosinophils (different quantities, same direction)

engagement.model: Rat allergic airway inflammation (lung oedema; thymic involution as systemic index)

engagement.judgement: Second compound from the same rat model, same direction: the lung anti-inflammatory readout (FeNO) fell at 58, 250 and 800 µg once daily. GW870086 (GSK mouse track) reported no airway PD biomarker in its asthma trial (Bareille 2013, abstract), so the mouse track is absent from this cell.

dose.model: Rat allergic airway inflammation (lung oedema; thymic involution as systemic index)

dose.quote: Further optimization of inhaled drug properties provided a second, equally potent, candidate, 15m (AZD7594), that demonstrated an improved therapeutic ratio over the benchmark inhaled corticosteroid 3 (fluticasone propionate) and prolonged the inhibition of lung edema, indicating potential for once-daily treatment.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the rat exposure numbers behind the therapeutic ratio are in the paywalled full text and were not read. Opener dated by proxy to NCT00963183 (posted 2009-08-21).
dose.judgement: The model stated a regimen (once daily, from prolonged oedema inhibition) and a margin (lung efficacy at less thymic involution than FP) but no human exposure number; dose is therefore scored on regimen and margin.

dose.model: Rat allergic airway inflammation (lung oedema; thymic involution as systemic index)

Healthy-volunteer studies showed dose-related cortisol suppression at higher nebulised doses (Prothon 2022), i.e. the margin is finite, not absent.

dose.model: Rat allergic airway inflammation (lung oedema; thymic involution as systemic index)

The tolerability half of the margin still held (day-84 cortisol AUEC ratio 0.916 vs placebo, p=0.285), which is why margin_stated stays true; the shortfall was efficacy at the tolerated top dose (74% of fluticasone furoate's effect), i.e. the therapeutic-ratio claim over-predicted the lung side.

AMP bronchoprovocation is a different human system from the allergen-induced late asthmatic response (different stimulus, mast-cell/AHR readout rather than late-phase eosinophilic response, steroid-naive subjects), so it is its own track per the track-identity rule; it was the earliest human model run for any member of this class. In dose it stated a regimen (1 mg once daily, effect to 12 h) and a tolerability margin (no cortisol or osteocalcin suppression), not an exposure target.

Patients were dosed to that regimen for 28 days without that toxicity and the FEV1 primary was null, so the dose row is 'reached, failed': contra derived from efficacy, counted once, with margin_stated true because the tolerability half held. No exposure or occupancy target was set, so the comparison is on regimen only.

The primary (trough FEV1, week 12) was not met at any dose while the ICS comparator was (+0.111 L, p=0.014); the rat model's claim of an improved therapeutic ratio over FP therefore over-predicted lung efficacy at the tolerated top dose. Scored contra on the primary-endpoint rule with magnitude direction_only (FEV1 rose dose-dependently, ~74% of FF's effect). efficacy.note: GW870086 matched fluticasone propionate in mouse OVA allergic airway inflammation while sparing MMTV transactivation; GSK took it into asthma in 2005.

The same paper's in-vitro dissociation (MMTV transactivation antagonised, cytokine repression retained) is the mechanistic premise, not a disease model.

efficacy.note: GW870086 1 mg once daily for 28 days in 36 mild-moderate asthmatics: FEV1 -0.077 L vs placebo, no effect on PEF or rescue use.

Contra dated to the paper (epub 2013-10-01, print December 2013); Uings 2013 and Bareille 2013 are the same year, so the strip opens and fails in 2013 on the published record. Caveat: 1 mg may have been under-dosed (its allergen-challenge protection was half of FP's, see the challenge track), which is why dose on this track stays untested rather than doubling the count.

AstraZeneca took it into COPD instead (Kuna 2017, https://doi.org/10.1111/bcpt.12768; 353 patients, no lung-function effect), which is another disease and does not score here. strengthens marks a second uncompared use of the same model, not a status change.

The model's number fell below the class bar and the drug failed, which is neg, not contra. safety.model: AMP (adenosine monophosphate) bronchoprovocation in steroid-naive mild asthmatics (human challenge)
safety.population: Steroid-naive mild asthmatics (challenge); mild-moderate asthmatics (28-day trial)
safety.note: The same 7-day crossover read 24-h urinary cortisol and serum osteocalcin as the systemic-GR index beside the airway readout.
safety.short: AMP study read cortisol and osteocalcin
safety.quote: Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, 3-way Crossover Study to Investigate the Effect of 7-days Repeat Once Daily Inhaled Doses of GW870086X Administered Via DISKHALER on Airway Responsiveness to AMP in Mild Steroid-naive Male Asthmatics
safety.confidence_note: Registry record (tier 3) used as the proxy opener, as the draft does for this NCT; dosing actually began 2005-10-07 (CT.gov actual start) and the record was first posted 2007-06-07. No results were ever posted; the result appeared only as Leaker 2015.
safety.judgement: GSK ran GW870086X 1 and 3 mg once daily for 7 days against placebo in a 20-subject (17 completers) three-way crossover reading PC20 AMP, FeNO, urinary cortisol and osteocalcin (SIG102335, 2005-06). AMP bronchoprovocation is a different human system from the allergen-induced late asthmatic response (different stimulus, mast-cell/AHR readout rather than late-phase eosinophilic response, steroid-naive subjects), so it is its own track per the track-identity rule; it was the earliest human model run for any member of this class. Its safety prediction (systemic sparing at effective doses) was published only in 2015 and has no patient-side comparison read.

safety.model: AMP (adenosine monophosphate) bronchoprovocation in steroid-naive mild asthmatics (human challenge)
safety.population: Steroid-naive mild asthmatics (challenge); mild-moderate asthmatics (28-day trial)
safety.note: Seven days of 1-3 mg left urinary cortisol and osteocalcin unchanged; the letter predicts reduced bone and metabolic AEs. No 28-day patient comparison read.
safety.quote: There was no reduction in cortisol or osteocalcin after 7 days of repeat dosing with GW870086X. These data support the potential for reduced bone and metabolic AEs with GW870086X.
safety.confidence_note: The model states a safety prediction (systemic sparing at 1-3 mg) but no patient-side record of cortisol or bone markers after 28 days of GW870086 was read (Bareille 2013 J Asthma abstract carries no safety detail; the Curr Drug Ther papers are blocked), so the prediction stays uncompared.
safety.reason: Sparing predicted; no patient record read
safety.judgement: Second uncompared use of the same model's safety readout, marked strengthens rather than a status change: the stated prediction (no cortisol or osteocalcin suppression at effective doses) exists from 2015 but the only GW870086 patient trials read report no systemic-GR markers, so the cell cannot be scored.
